# Results — Study 418 (Money Flow Index) on the real SPY tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — a 14-day
oscillator long/flat timing rule (indicator ≤ 30 → long, ≥ 70 → flat, else hold) run on
the **Money Flow Index** (volume-weighted) and the **plain RSI**, with one execution lag
(decide at *t*'s close, earn *t+1*'s return), flat = cash, one-way costs × NAV, and all
returns measured **excess-of-cash** so the race is excess-vs-excess. Raced against
buy-and-hold SPY. As-of **2026-06-23**; history back to 2000-01-03 (the partial
2026-06-24 bar is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | 2000-01-03 to 2026-06-23 | 6,657 | `0e5348c18f0c` |

SPY auto-adjusted daily OHLCV from yfinance — `close` is split/dividend-adjusted
(total-return-ish), `volume` is the raw traded share count (what the MFI weights by).

## The race — net excess-of-cash Sharpe (2 bps one-way costs)

| Arm | net Sharpe | ann. return | HAC *t* | max DD | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MFI** (volume-weighted) | **0.460** | +7.23% | **+2.72** | −52.96% | 41.7% |
| RSI (plain) | 0.312 | +5.14% | +1.93 | −55.19% | 39.6% |
| Buy & hold SPY | **0.505** | +9.76% | +3.02 | −55.19% | 100% |

- The MFI's own book clears the inference bar (HAC *t* = +2.72 ≥ 2) — but it is long
  only ~42% of a market that drifted up ~10%/yr, so the *t* is **recycled beta**, not a
  volume edge.
- **Both timers lose to buy-and-hold** (0.505): stepping aside on overbought readings
  cost more return than it saved in risk. Delta MFI − buy-hold = **−0.045** Sharpe.
- The MFI does edge the plain RSI (**Δ = +0.148** Sharpe) — the question this study
  exists to answer — but see the head-to-head test below.

## The head-to-head — is "MFI beats RSI" real? (block bootstrap)

The MFI-minus-RSI **daily net-excess difference**, block-bootstrapped (21-day blocks,
2,000 draws):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed daily diff mean | 8.28e-05 |
| observed Δ Sharpe (MFI − RSI) | +0.148 |
| two-sided bootstrap *p* | **0.277** |

The +0.148 Sharpe advantage of the volume-weighted RSI over the plain RSI is **well
inside the noise band** — the defining promise of the MFI is statistically invisible on
SPY.

## Block-permutation placebo — is the *timing* informative?

Shuffle each book's position in contiguous 21-day blocks against realised returns
(keeps time-in-market, destroys alignment); *p* = P(shuffled mean ≥ observed):

| arm | permutation *p* |
|---|--:|
| MFI | **0.030** |
| RSI | 0.204 |

The MFI's timing is *marginally* informative (volume does a little something); the RSI's
is not. But "a little something" that still can't beat the RSI head-to-head or
buy-and-hold does not earn an INVESTABLE stamp.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (net excess Sharpe)

| one-way cost | MFI Sharpe | MFI HAC *t* | RSI Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | 0.466 | +2.76 | 0.314 |
| 2.0 bps | 0.460 | +2.72 | 0.312 |
| 5.0 bps | 0.451 | +2.67 | 0.309 |
| 10.0 bps | 0.436 | +2.59 | 0.304 |

Turnover is low, so costs barely move the lines — and **both timers stay below
buy-and-hold (0.505) at every cost level, including zero.** This is not an edge eaten by
frictions; it is no edge to begin with.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a *planted, volume-keyed*
overreaction (down-moves on heavy volume bounce harder). Net excess Sharpe, seed 418:

| planted edge | MFI Sharpe | RSI Sharpe | Δ (MFI − RSI) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (no volume edge) | +0.365 | +0.560 | −0.195 |
| 1.0 | +0.490 | +0.196 | +0.294 |
| 2.0 | +0.432 | +0.183 | +0.249 |

When a volume-keyed bounce is present, the MFI pulls clearly ahead of the RSI (across 12
seeds at edge = 2 the mean Δ is **+0.164**); with no volume edge the RSI is fine. The
machinery *can* detect a volume edge — SPY's volume simply doesn't carry one. (A
synthetic control proves the harness, never the real-tape stamp.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The MFI's net excess book is positive at HAC *t* = +2.72 (clears
  2), but the placebo and the buy-hold comparison show the *t* is bull-market exposure,
  not a volume signal. The literature sells the MFI as "a better RSI"; this tape can't
  certify even that it *differs* from the RSI.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Buy-and-hold (0.505) beats both timers at every cost level
  including zero; the rule converts beta into *less* beta. Nothing to deploy.
- **"Beats the plain RSI?" — NOT SUPPORTED.** Δ = +0.148 Sharpe, block-bootstrap
  *p* = 0.277. The volume weighting changes the answer by a rounding error on SPY.
